clue.text: Rabble-rouser encouraged to consume health food

indicators.note: to consume is to take something in, so one word swallows the other here

parts.note: to fire someone up is to encourage them, so encouraged gives FIRED
bran is the classic fibre-rich health food

explanation.surface: A stirring agitator is urged on to eat something wholesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encouraged' reads as describing the rabble-rouser, but it is the outer word, as in 'fired up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person who stirs up trouble or agitates a crowd is called by this word.

clue.text: Puncture on curve? (Not new lorry)

parts.note: a puncture leaves you with a flat tyre, called a flat

indicators.note: not new tells us to drop the letter standing for new from the word before it

parts.note: a bend is a curve in a road

explanation.surface: A driver wonders whether a flat tyre happened on a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not new' removes N from BEND to leave BED; the brackets hide that 'lorry' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a truck with an open, flat loading platform and no sides is this kind of lorry.

clue.text: What's chap never poked into flower? Probably not this!

definitions.text: What's chap never poked into flower? Probably not this!

indicators.note: poked into means pushed inside, so these letters go within the flower word

parts.note: a rose is a flower
a chap is a man
no can mean never, as in 'no way'

explanation.surface: A joke about which nose a man would avoid sticking into a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a man with such a prominent hooked nose might be wise not to push it into a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hooked or aquiline nose is named after profiles on old coins of Rome.

clue.text: Raised money when one's short

indicators.note: short here means lacking, so the word for money goes without the letter for one

parts.note: bread is slang for money
A means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: Someone collected funds while one person was out of pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's short' means the A (one) is missing from BREAD. 'Raised' looks like 'raised money' but it is the definition, as in a child raised by parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bring up children or animals is to raise or breed them, past tense matching.

clue.text: A substantial cut limiting grant affecting sporting activities?

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing on both sides, so one piece sits inside the other
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: thick means substantial or bulky
to let is to grant or allow

explanation.surface: A big funding cut hits a sports grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the final letter, leaving THIC; 'grant' looks like money in the surface but means allow.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to sport and physical exercise is what this adjective means; the question mark marks a loose phrasing.

clue.text: Boil half-lanced? Sitting upright month later

indicators.note: later puts the month after the first piece
in a down entry, sitting upright means the letters are read from bottom to top
half here picks the second three of the six letters of lanced

parts.note: Oct is short for October

explanation.surface: A boil has been half lanced; the patient sits up a month on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the back half of 'lanced'; in a down light 'Sitting upright' reads it bottom to top. 'Boil' looks like the swelling but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to extract the essence of something by boiling it down is to perform this process.

clue.text: A little difficulty? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite tells us to drop the final letter of the word

parts.note: a scrape is a tight spot or difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a problem is minor and is told it is not quite so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' docks the last letter of SCRAPE. 'A little' is the definition, as in 'not a scrap of evidence'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tiny fragment or small amount of something, as in a scrap of paper.

clue.text: Rock fan involved in scandal with REM

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan of the band R.E.M. is caught up in a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges SCANDAL plus REM; R.E.M. is a real rock band, which hides that REM is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone who dances violently into others at rock or punk concerts is a kind of fan.

clue.text: Defiant, unpleasant expression raised about book

indicators.note: about means going round, so the letters surround the book letter
in a down entry, raised means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a leer is a nasty, knowing look

explanation.surface: A defiant person's sneer is lifted around a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns LEER into REEL, and 'about' wraps that round B.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, the word describes someone resisting authority, as in rebel forces.

clue.text: Queen latterly shunning drawing-rooms considered high-risk

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so that letter is removed

parts.note: parlours are old-fashioned sitting rooms or drawing-rooms

indicators.note: latterly picks out the final letter of the abbreviation for queen

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen avoids sitting rooms thought to be dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latterly' takes R, the end of ER (Elizabeth Regina), and 'shunning' removes it from PARLOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something perilous or precarious, full of danger, is described this way.

clue.text: Body part's injury (not head)

indicators.note: not head tells us to drop the first letter of the word

parts.note: harm is injury or damage

explanation.surface: A body part is hurt, but not the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not head' removes H from HARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the upper limb from shoulder to hand is one part of the body.

clue.text: What about confectionery warning signal? It's a sound arrangement

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the exclamation goes round the sweet word

parts.note: eh? is said when asking 'what?'
choc is short for chocolate
amber is the traffic light that warns drivers to stop

explanation.surface: Someone queries a sweet, then a warning light flashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What?' is the exclamation 'eh?'. Amber is the British name for the yellow traffic light that warns drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a chamber built to make sound reverberate is an arrangement for sound; also an environment repeating views.

clue.text: Subject of crack beginning to belabour individual

indicators.note: beginning to points at the first letter of the following word

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A cracked joke starts a lecture about one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes B from 'belabour'. 'crack' suggests a joke or a try, but here it is a fracture.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fracture is a crack, and the skeleton's hard parts are what break.

clue.text: Police caught lad misbehaving — a minor fault

indicators.note: misbehaving means behaving badly, so the letters run out of order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Officers nab a youngster for a small offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges POLICE, C and LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small sin or trifling offence is called by this Spanish-derived word.

clue.text: Drain once demolished over litre of hormonal material

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first piece sits above the second
demolished means knocked down, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An old drain is knocked down above a litre of liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' rearranges DRAIN ONCE, and 'over' puts that above L in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The glands secreting hormones into the blood form a system, and this adjective relates to it.

clue.text: Dead item — dead before being eaten by a lion on the rampage

indicators.note: being eaten by means taken inside, so this letter pair goes within the rearranged letters
on the rampage means running wild, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: or is an old word for before, as in 'or ever'

explanation.surface: Something dead is about to be eaten by a rampaging lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rampage' turns A LION into ONAIL. 'Or' meaning before is archaic, as in 'or ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'dead as a' this metal stud is a stock comparison, so the item stands for deadness.

clue.text: Sponsors requiring slight change to opinions

indicators.note: a slight change here shifts one letter to a new spot in the word

parts.note: angles are points of view or opinions

explanation.surface: Backers need their views tweaked a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slight change to' moves the E in ANGLES one place left.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: backers who finance theatre productions or start-ups are called by this heavenly word.

clue.text: Effort expending one bit of energy while holding to force

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the remaining letters wrap round the word
expending means using up, so the letter is spent and removed

parts.note: exertion means physical or mental effort
E is the symbol for energy, and only one of the two in the word is lost

explanation.surface: Effort burns energy while holding something under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expending' loses only one of the two Es, the second, leaving EXRTION to hold the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: obtaining something by threats or coercion is this crime, so force fits.

clue.text: Greek character embracing love and weird sex with us in bubbly style

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the Greek letter goes round the love letter

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
O is love, a zero score in tennis

indicators.note: weird means strange, so these letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek with love and odd sex games, all in fizzy style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' rearranges the five letters into SSEUX; love is O from the zero score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: French term for sparkling wine; it describes a drink made fizzy, so bubbly style fits.

clue.text: Cat article omitted from main collection

indicators.note: omitted from means left out of, so the article is removed

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea or ocean
an is the indefinite article
a lot is a collection or batch at auction

explanation.surface: An item is missing from the main collection of a catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the poetic word for the open sea, not 'chief'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a spotted wild cat of Central and South America.

clue.text: Superhero, without hesitation, represented as Classical figure

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A superhero, shown without stalling, is recast as an ancient figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes ER out of SUPERHERO, and 'represented' rearranges the remaining SUPHERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the legendary musician of Greek myth who sought his wife in the underworld.

clue.text: Indigenous movement fronted by cheats receiving money

indicators.note: fronted by means the following piece comes after the first
receiving means taking in, so the money letter goes inside

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them, so cheats gives DOES
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A native gesture led by swindlers taking cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheats' is a verb here: to 'do' someone is to swindle them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: native to a country rather than foreign, as in domestic produce.

clue.text: Grain is hot in description of Riviera

parts.note: corn is grain
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Grain is hot on the sunny coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cornish Riviera is the nickname for the sunny south coast of Cornwall, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this adjective names the English coast nicknamed a riviera, so it describes that riviera.

clue.text: Second vehicle carrying one German mathematician

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the bus holds the one

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A second bus carries a German maths man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' as in 'wait a mo', a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: August Möbius, the German who described the one-sided twisted strip.

clue.text: Energetic person who's working with Europe

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone lively at work alongside Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the letters of WHOS and EUROPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a dynamic, forceful person full of energy is described with this word for a generating station.

clue.text: Victorian painter's power

definitions.meaning: G.F. ... was a Victorian painter and sculptor

explanation.surface: An artist of the 1800s and his influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a Victorian artist's surname, and the plural of the unit measuring power.

clue.text: Moroccan tree, Arabic twice over

indicators.note: twice over means the abbreviation appears two times in a row

explanation.surface: A North African tree's name is Arabic, said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the sandarac tree of North Africa, a conifer, is known by this name.

clue.text: Historic stringed instrument: some forgery likely to turn up

indicators.note: in a down entry, to turn up means the letters are read upwards
some means a part of, so the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: An old stringed instrument turns out probably fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds ERYL in 'forgery likely', and 'to turn up' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the harp-like instrument of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Over a large amount — product of eleven and sixty, perhaps

indicators.note: a product is something made from materials, so these words are remade into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Multiplying eleven by sixty gives a big number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product of' looks like multiplication but rearranges ELEVEN and SIXTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: widely, covering a large area or range, as in travelled extensively.

clue.text: New Zealander heading off Maori group

indicators.note: heading off means losing the front, so the first letter goes

parts.note: kiwi is the nickname for a New Zealander

explanation.surface: A New Zealander leaves a Maori tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes K from KIWI.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Maori word for a tribe or people, a large social unit.

clue.text: Fibre is twisted, one extracted from canvas

indicators.note: twisted means turned round, so the little word is read backwards
extracted from means pulled out of, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: a sail is made of canvas, and canvas can mean the sails
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fibre is twisted with one thread pulled out of the canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns IS into SI, and 'extracted from' takes I out of SAIL to leave SAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a strong plant fibre from agave, used for ropes and matting.

clue.text: Adolescent's birthday — partying for it, then sex

indicators.note: partying suggests wild behaviour, so these letters run riot

explanation.surface: A teenager's birthday: a party, then sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partying for' rearranges IT THEN SEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the birthday marking sixteen years, a milestone teenage age.
